title: P02 follow-up: Muon momentum warmup 0.85 -> 0.95 over the first 300 steps on the 081 Polar Express Muon incumbent
description: P02 follow-up: ramp Muon's Nesterov momentum linearly from 0.85 to 0.95 over the first 300 of ~4700 pretraining steps (modded-nanogpt convention), everything else identical to the 081-claude incumbent. Val loss reaches its plateau (~0.095) within the first ~60 s (~750 steps), so the early trajectory sets the generalizing features that expert iteration must extend past length 6; less stale momentum while gradients rotate fastest should give a better early solution and a better RL starting point.
hypothesis: With constant beta 0.95 the Muon direction averages ~20 steps of gradients from the rapidly changing early landscape (and the LR warmup is only 200 steps), so the first few hundred orthogonalized updates point partly along stale directions. A lower initial beta tracks the current gradient more closely, reaching the val-loss plateau sooner and at a slightly better point; since 081's val loss is flat from ~60 s onward, the representation formed early is what the fixed AdamW RL stage extends. Mechanism is confined to the first ~20 s of a 300 s budget, so any effect should be small.
expected_delta: -20 to +20 theorems at >=7 on the 3-seed mean (central ~+3); pretraining steps and final val loss within noise of 081 (4682/4732/4769 steps; val 0.095/0.091/0.096); no change in RL sampling speed or total wall-clock

arch.change: none versus 081-claude: 5 untied fork GPT blocks, d_model 256, 8 heads (head dim 32), d_ff 1024, RoPE base 10000, LayerNorm, GELU, untied embedding/readout
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) from the fork; model.cfg records n_layer=5 and the state dict has blocks.0-blocks.4
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (5 per sample), unchanged fork code

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization and 300-step momentum warmup 0.85->0.95 on hidden matrices and head.weight; AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 081-claude)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: unchanged from 081-claude: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2 (070-claude: 1), head (99,256) 1. Every Muon update now has element RMS ~1/16 times lr; only fc2's step doubles.
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) plus head.weight (99,256; vocab 99, no bias) are in Muon: 21 matrices. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 and head are orthogonalized whole. head is wide (99<256) so it is not transposed and its update has 99 singular values near 1.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: unchanged from 081-claude: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: unchanged from 081-claude: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

momentum_warmup.change: CHANGED versus 081-claude: Muon Nesterov momentum beta ramps linearly from 0.85 at step 0 to 0.95 at step 300, then stays 0.95 (081-claude: constant 0.95 from step 1). beta = 0.85 + 0.10 * min(step / 300, 1), used for both the momentum-buffer lerp and the Nesterov lookahead lerp.
momentum_warmup.source: modded-nanogpt speedrun convention (Muon momentum warmup 0.85 -> 0.95 over the first 300 steps)
momentum_warmup.scope: Muon matrices only; AdamW auxiliary betas unchanged (0.9, 0.95); LR warmup (200 steps) and cosine schedule unchanged

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 21 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: unchanged from 081-claude: fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero. Same per-seed RNG streams.

objective.change: none versus 081-claude: plain fork loss_on cross-entropy on proof tokens (093-claude's entropy penalty is not present)
